total_mass.quote: The total mass of the asteroid belt is estimated to be 2.39×10^21 kg, which is 3% of the mass of the Moon.

mass_in_four_largest.quote: The four largest objects, Ceres, Vesta, Pallas, and Hygiea, contain an estimated 62% of the belt's total mass, with 39% accounted for by Ceres alone.

count_over_1km.quote: the asteroid belt has between 700,000 and 1.7 million asteroids with a diameter of 1 km or more.

count_over_100km.quote: Over 200 asteroids are larger than 100 km

average_spacing.quote: On average the distance between the asteroids is about 965,600 km (600,000 miles).

edges.quote: The 4:1 orbital resonance at 2.06 AU marks the inner boundary; 2:1 at 3.27 AU.

class_shares.quote: Carbonaceous asteroids comprise over 75% of the visible asteroids; S-type asteroids form about 17% of the total asteroid population; M-types most of the remainder.

family_share.quote: About 33% to 35% of asteroids in the main belt are family members.

families.quote: There are about 20 to 30 reliably recognized families, with several tens of less certain groupings.

family_lifetime.quote: Asteroid families are thought to have lifetimes of the order of a billion years

count_over_1km.quote: The total number of Jupiter trojans larger than 1 km in diameter is believed to be about 1 million.

spread.unit: degrees along the orbit, each swarm
spread.quote: Each swarm stretches for about 26° along the orbit of Jupiter, amounting to a total distance of about 2.5 AU.

mass.quote: The total mass of the Jupiter trojans is estimated at 0.0001 of the mass of Earth or one-fifth of the mass of the asteroid belt.

class.quote: The Jupiter trojans mostly are D-type asteroids

albedo.quote: The average value is 0.056 ± 0.003 for the objects larger than 57 km.

edges.quote: The main body of the belt is generally accepted to extend from the 2:3 mean-motion resonance at 39.5 AU to the 1:2 resonance at roughly 48 AU.

count_over_100km.quote: more than 100000 KBOs over 100 km (62 mi) in diameter are thought to exist.

mass.quote: The most recent estimate (2018) puts the total mass of the Kuiper belt at (1.97±0.30)×10−2 Earth masses.

thickness.unit: degrees either side of the plane
thickness.quote: The Kuiper belt is quite thick, with the main concentration extending as much as ten degrees outside the ecliptic plane

share_asteroids.quote: Among asteroids, an estimated 2% would have satellites.

share_outer.quote: Among trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs), an estimated 11% are thought to be binary or multiple objects.

separation.quote: The distances of the components for the known binaries vary from a few hundreds of kilometres to more than 3000 km for the asteroids.

by_type.quote: Chondrites 86.2% (ordinary 80.0%, carbonaceous 4.4%, enstatite 1.6%); achondrites 8.2%; stony-iron 1.0%; iron 4.6%.

note: Fetched 2026-10-04. Each quote is as a page-reading tool returned it; the figures were not checked against the pages by eye.
